rendering.title: Bacterial ancestor of the mitochondrion
rendering.body:
Mitochondria have two membranes — an outer and an inner — and this unusual feature is a direct clue to how they came to exist inside cells.

The endosymbiotic theory explains it this way:

About 1.5 to 2 billion years ago, an ancestral eukaryotic cell engulfed a free-living aerobic bacterium, but instead of digesting it, the cell kept it alive. Over many generations, this bacterium became a permanent resident — an endosymbiont — eventually losing the ability to live independently. That ancient bacterium is the ancestor of every mitochondrion alive today.

Now consider where the two membranes come from:
- The inner membrane is the original bacterial plasma membrane. It is the one that carries the electron transport chain and ATP synthase, just as those proteins sat in the bacterial membrane before engulfment.
- The outer membrane is derived from the host cell's engulfing membrane (the phagosomal membrane that wrapped around the bacterium).

So the double-membrane structure is not a design feature — it is a fossil of the engulfment event.

Several other lines of evidence support this story:
1. Mitochondria have their own circular DNA, resembling bacterial chromosomes far more than the linear chromosomes of the eukaryotic nucleus.
2. Mitochondrial ribosomes are 70S (bacterial size), not the 80S ribosomes found in the cytoplasm.
3. Mitochondria divide by binary fission, the same way bacteria divide.
4. The closest living relatives of mitochondria among bacteria are the alphaproteobacteria (particularly the Rickettsiales group).

Most mitochondrial proteins are now encoded by the nuclear genome and imported after the fact — the result of gene transfer from the endosymbiont to the host nucleus over evolutionary time. Only a small number of proteins are still encoded in mitochondrial DNA itself.
rendering.summary: An ancestral eukaryotic cell engulfed an aerobic bacterium. Over time this became a permanent endosymbiont, retaining its own DNA and double membrane.
rendering.hint: If the inner membrane comes from the original bacterium, what would you predict about which membrane hosts the proteins of the electron transport chain?
